title: Flat fibre-product stalk rings and pullback comparison
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], their total derived functors computed by K-flat resolutions with flat terms and K-injective resolutions, and K-flat derived tensor product. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms, and set $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. For a geometric point $\bar x':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X'$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, write $\bar x=g'\bar x'$, $\bar y'=f'\bar x'$, $\bar y=f\bar x$, and put $R=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y',\bar y'}$, $C=\mathcal O_{X',\bar x'}$, $D=A\otimes_R B$. The stalks are colimits over pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods, and $D\to C$ is induced by the projection stalk maps. The canonical ring map $D\to C$ is flat, meaning that tensoring with $C$ over $D$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For every complex $M^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules there are canonical identifications
$$( (g')^*M^\bullet)_{\bar x'}\cong M^\bullet_{\bar x}\otimes_A C,\qquad (L(g')^*M^\bullet)_{\bar x'}\cong M^\bullet_{\bar x}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C.$$
The second is an isomorphism in $D(C)$; the first is an isomorphism of complexes. Under these identifications the derived-to-ordinary pullback map is the canonical derived-to-ordinary scalar-extension map. No flatness of $f$ or $g$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose an affine pointed etale chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}r\to Y$ at $\bar y$. Base change to $X_V=X\times_YV$ and $Y'_V=Y'\times_YV$, and choose affine pointed etale scheme charts $U=\operatorname{Spec}a\to X_V$ and $V'=\operatorname{Spec}b\to Y'_V$ lifting the fixed geometric points. Fibre products exist and etale covers pull back by lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers; atlases and their affine restrictions exist by def-trf-algebraic-space. Lifts over $\Omega$ exist because a nonempty etale fibre over an algebraically closed field has an $\Omega$-point. By the composition and arbitrary algebraic-space base-change assertions for representable etale morphisms in lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests, $U\to X$ and $V'\to Y'$ are etale. Set $W=U\times_VV'=\operatorname{Spec}(a\otimes_r b)$, with the point induced by the chosen lifts. The map $W\to X_V\times_VY'_V=X'\times_YV$ factors as $U\times_VV'\to X_V\times_VV'\to X_V\times_VY'_V$. Each arrow is a base change of one of the etale chart maps, so composition gives an etale map $W\to X'\times_YV$ and then $W\to X'$, composing with the base change $X'\times_YV\to X'$ of $V\to Y$, by lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests. Here the affine fibre product is computed by the tensor-product universal property. All four lifted points use the original $\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 0DKG, lemma-single-complex-base-change-condition, etale chart diagram; spaces.tex Tag 02X2; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 05W3

proof.text: Put $t=a\otimes_r b$. The chart identifications of lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness identify $R,A,B,C$ with the strict henselizations of the local rings of $V,U,V',W$ at their lifted points. By lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples, applied to the corresponding primes of $r,a,b,t$, the canonical maps $r\to R$, $a\to A$, $b\to B$, $t\to C$ are ind-etale. These are the actual chart-to-stalk maps: both descriptions send an etale-neighbourhood section to its germ. In particular their structural maps commute with the maps induced by $U\to V$, $V'\to V$ and the projections of $W$.

Let $a_R=a\otimes_rR$ and $b_R=b\otimes_rR$. By base change in lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability, $a\to a_R$ and $b\to b_R$ are ind-etale. The canonical maps $a_R\to A$ and $b_R\to B$ exist because the stalk maps agree on $r$. Since $a_R,A$ are ind-etale over $a$, and $b_R,B$ are ind-etale over $b$, permanence in that same node shows these canonical maps are ind-etale. Base change and composition now show that
$$t\longrightarrow t\otimes_rR\cong a_R\otimes_Rb_R\longrightarrow A\otimes_Rb_R\longrightarrow A\otimes_RB=D$$
is ind-etale. The first arrow is the base change of $r\to R$; the last two are the base changes of $a_R\to A$ and $b_R\to B$. Thus $D$ and $C$ are both ind-etale $t$-algebras. The tensor universal property makes the projection-stalk map $D\to C$ a $t$-algebra map. Permanence gives that it is ind-etale and hence weakly etale. By def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra, a weakly etale ring map is in particular flat. This proves the asserted exactness without requiring either $f$ or $g$ to be flat. Notice that $D$ was never assumed local or identified with $C$.

source.place: Tags 097J, 097K, 097M and 097N, lemmas base-change-ind-etale, composition-ind-etale, ind-etale-permanence and ind-etale-implies

proof.text: Write $h=g'$ and $p$ for the point $\bar x'$ of $X'_{\mathrm{et}}$; its image point is $q=hp=\bar x$. The tensor-pullback definition gives $h^*F=h^{-1}F\otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_{X'}$. Apply lem-sfb-ringed-site-point-tensor, in degree zero, to the point $p$ of the ringed site with ring sheaf $h^{-1}\mathcal O_X$. The stalk of this ring is $A$, the stalk of $h^{-1}F$ is $F_q$, and that of $\mathcal O_{X'}$ is $C$. These first two identifications are inverse-image composition $p^{-1}h^{-1}=(hp)^{-1}$; the normalized module actions are those of def-sfb-ringed-site-point. Consequently $(h^*F)_p\cong F_q\otimes_AC$, carrying the germ of a local tensor $m\otimes c$ to $[m]\otimes[c]$. Applying this natural identification in each degree commutes with the differentials, which send $m\otimes c$ to $d(m)\otimes c$. This proves the first identification as an isomorphism of complexes, for every $M^\bullet$.

Let $u:P^\bullet\to M^\bullet$ be the K-flat resolution with flat terms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules by which the statement's convention computes $Lh^*M^\bullet$. The stalk criterion lem-sfb-ringed-site-kflat-stalk-criterion gives that $P_q^\bullet$ is K-flat over $A$. By lem-sfb-ringed-site-point-exact, $u_q:P_q^\bullet\to M_q^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism: an exact additive functor preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology. Hence $P_q^\bullet\otimes_AC$ represents $M_q^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C$. On the sheaf side $h^*P^\bullet$ represents $Lh^*M^\bullet$ by its stipulated K-flat construction; its exact stalk represents $(Lh^*M^\bullet)_p$. Step 4 identifies this representing complex with $P_q^\bullet\otimes_AC$. Localizing this chain isomorphism gives the asserted isomorphism in $D(C)$. No boundedness or quasi-coherence is used.

The derived-to-ordinary pullback map on the chosen representative is $h^*u:h^*P^\bullet\to h^*M^\bullet$. Naturality of the chain identification in step 4 sends its stalk to $u_q\otimes_A1_C:P_q^\bullet\otimes_AC\to M_q^\bullet\otimes_AC$; on local pure tensors both maps send $[m]\otimes[c]$ to $[u(m)]\otimes[c]$. The source represents derived scalar extension by step 5, so this is exactly its canonical derived-to-ordinary comparison. The formulas commute with morphisms and quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat resolutions, since the same formula holds for every chain map. They therefore give the canonical identifications and comparison independently of the chosen representative.
